title: Lighter arguments against the creation and infusion of the soul are dissolved
pass_a_gloss:
Article IX. Lighter arguments commonly brought against the creation and infusion of the soul are dissolved.
1. First objection: God completed the whole work of creation in the first six days and afterward rested from his work (Gen 2; Exod 20); therefore new souls are not now created. Answer: after the sixth day God ceased from creating new species, not new individuals; but the souls he now creates differ from Adam's soul, which he first created, not in species but in number.
2. Second: Genesis 5 says Adam begot a son in his image; but a son is the image and likeness of the father according to the soul; therefore Adam begot a son according to the soul. Answer: a son is the image and likeness of the father not so much by reason of the soul as by reason of the whole supposit — that is, insofar as he is something consisting of soul and body. Adam therefore not only begot a son like the father, as Esthius holds, but also begot that in which that likeness chiefly consists, namely the very person of his son, composed of soul and body.
3. Third: Genesis 46 says seventy souls went out from Jacob's thigh, which is nothing other than to be translated by propagation of seed. Answer: souls are put synecdochically for humans; we can also add that the souls themselves went out from Jacob's thigh not as translated from Jacob's thigh as to their being simply, but as descending from it as to their existence in the body and union with the body; for the virtue of the seed that went out from Jacob's thigh effected the union of body and soul.
4. Fourth: if a human by generating does not produce a rational soul, he is of worse condition than brutes and plants, which produce souls proper to themselves — namely vegetative and sensitive. Esthius answers that a human is of better condition even in the office of generating than brutes or plants are, because his generative power reaches to the union of the noblest form with matter, as declared above. Add that it itself belongs to great dignity to have such a soul that, because of its excellence, no power of nature can reach to producing it; for which reason not even to angels, whose nature is more excellent than humans', does any power of generating belong.
5. Fifth: if a human does not generate the child's soul but the body, he does not generate the whole human but another part of him — indeed the less noble part. Answer: deny the sequel. Mary did not beget Christ's deity, and yet is truly said to have begotten the whole Christ; fire also, when from wood it generates other fire, does not generate the matter of that fire but only the form, and yet is said to generate or produce that whole fire; according to Aristotle's definition, generation is a change of the whole, etc. So here distinguish between the whole human and the whole of the human; for the father generates the whole human — that is, all the parts.
6. Sixth: if God creates one by one the souls of all who are begotten in any way, he cooperates with fornicators and adulterers: for he creates and grants souls to fornicating and adulterous conceptions, which seems absurd. Answer: God cooperates with natural generation, which is good of itself and a work of nature — not with the vice by which fornicators and adulterers complete generation against God's law.
pass_b_english: Article IX. Lighter arguments against the creation and infusion of the soul are dissolved.

1. Objection: God finished creation in six days and rested (Gen 2; Exod 20), so new souls are not now created. Answer: after the sixth day he ceased creating new species, not new individuals. Souls he now creates differ from Adam's first-created soul in number, not in species.

2. Genesis 5: Adam begot a son in his image; a son is the father's image according to the soul; so Adam begot according to the soul. Answer: the likeness is chiefly of the whole person consisting of soul and body, not of the soul alone. Adam begot not only a like son but the very person composed of soul and body in which that likeness chiefly consists (Esthius).

3. Genesis 46: seventy souls went out from Jacob's thigh — supposedly translation by seed. Answer: souls stand synecdochically for humans. Or: souls went out from Jacob's thigh not as to simple being but as to existence in the body and union with it; the seed's virtue effected that union.

4. If generating does not produce a rational soul, humans are worse off than brutes and plants that produce their own vegetative and sensitive souls. Esthius: humans are better off even in generating, because generative power reaches the union of the noblest form with matter. It is dignity to have a soul so excellent that no natural power can produce it — which is why even angels have no generative power.

5. If the father generates only the body, he does not generate the whole human but the less noble part. Deny the sequel. Mary did not beget Christ's deity yet truly begot the whole Christ; fire from wood generates fire's form, not its matter, yet generates that whole fire (Aristotle: generation is change of the whole). Distinguish the whole human from the whole of the human: the father generates the whole human — all the parts.

6. If God creates each soul of whoever is begotten, he cooperates with fornicators and adulterers. Answer: God cooperates with natural generation, good of itself and nature's work — not with the vice by which they complete generation against his law.
source_text:
ART. IX.
Diluuntur leviora argumenta quae afferri solent contra creationem & infusionem animae.

1. Objicitur primo: DEUS sex primis diebus totum creationis opus absolvit, postea vero requievit ab opere suo, Gen. 2, Exod. 20; non igitur novae animae nunc creantur. Respond. DEUM post sextum diem cessasse a creatione novarum specierum, non vero novorum individuorum: animae autem, quas jam creat, non specie sed numero differunt ab anima Adami, quam primo creavit.

2. Secundo obj.: Genes. 5 dicitur Adam genuisse filium ad imaginem suam; est autem filius imago & similitudo patris secundum animam: Ergo Adam genuit filium secundum animam. Resp. filium esse imaginem & similitudinem patris non tam ratione animae quam ratione totius suppositi, i.e. quatenus est quid constans ex anima & corpore: Adam ergo non solum genuit filium similem patri, ut vult Esthius, sed etiam genuit id in quo illa similitudo potissimum consistit, videlicet ipsam personam filii sui, ex anima & corpore conflatam.

3. Tertio obj.: Genes. 46 dicuntur 70 animae egressae de femore Iacobi, quod non est aliud quam feminis propagatione traduci. Respond. animas synecdochice pro hominibus esse positas: addere etiam possumus, ipsas animas egressas fuisse ex femore Iacobi, non quod e femore Iacobi traductae sint quoad earum esse simpliciter, sed quod ex eo descenderint quoad earum existentiam in corpore & unionem cum corpore; virtus enim seminis egressi ex femore Iacobi effecit unionem corporis & animae.

4. Quarto obj.: si homo generando non producit animam rationalem, pejoris est conditionis quam bruta & plantae, quae producunt animas sibi proprias, videlicet vegetativam & sensitivam. Respondet Esthius, hominem esse melioris conditionis etiam in officio generandi quam sunt bruta aut plantae, eo quod vis ejus generativa pertingat ad unionem nobilissimae formae cum materia, ut supra declaratum est. Adde quod hoc ipsum ad magnam dignitatem pertinet, talem habere animam, ad quam producendam, propter ipsius excellentiam, nulla vis naturae possit pertingere; qua ratione nec angelis, quorum natura excellentior est quam hominum, vis ulla generandi competit.

5. Quinto obj.: si homo non generat animam filii sed corpus, non generat totum hominem, sed alteram ejus partem, imo ignobiliorem ejus partem. Resp. negando sequelam: Maria enim non genuit Deitatem CHRISTI, & tamen vere dicitur genuisse totum CHRISTUM: ignis etiam, cum ex ligno generat alium ignem, non generat materiam illius ignis, sed tantum formam, & tamen dicitur generare seu producere totum illum ignem; secundum definitionem Aristotelis, generatio est mutatio totius, &c. Quare hic distinguendum est inter totum hominem & totum hominis; pater enim generat totum hominem, id est, omnes partes.

6. Sexto obj.: si DEUS sigillatim creat animas omnium qui quomodocunque gignuntur, cooperatur scortatoribus & adulteris: nam fornicariis & adulterinis conceptibus animas creat & largitur, quod videtur absurdum. Resp. DEUS cooperatur generationi naturali, quae est per se bona & opus naturae; non autem vitio quo fornicatores & adulteri contra legem DEI generationem perficiunt.
